## RCA (Phase 1 complete) — proven root cause + attribution

**Mechanism (runtime-proven).** `export_tickets` in `src/rebar/_io/export_ndjson.py:168` serializes each export line with a RAW `json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False)`, never routing through the js-safe choke point (`rebar._mcp_errors.js_safe_dumps` / `js_safe_result`) that bug e127 (unhelping-creviced-rhino) established for the MCP + CLI `--output json` surfaces. So every `time.time_ns()` field (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `comments[].timestamp`, `signature.signed_at`) goes on the NDJSON wire as a bare 19-digit JSON integer > 2^53.

Reproduced at runtime (fresh store, one ticket + one comment): raw export line carried 3 unquoted >=16-digit integer tokens; `node -e JSON.parse('{"created_at":1787975097502255001}')` returns `1787975097502255000` — a silent -1 ns float64 round. Matches the e127 hazard exactly.

**Legitimacy = defect (parity).** The wire form is a documented contract: `ticket_state.schema.json` / `common.schema.json` describe these fields as 'emitted as a JSON STRING of decimal digits ... whenever the value falls outside JavaScript's safe-integer range'. Export is `allOf(ticket_state + schema_version)` yet emits bare numbers, diverging from that documented wire form. e127 established this exact remedy for the sibling surfaces; export was DELIBERATELY left out of e127's scope (separately-versioned interop projection with an import round-trip), which is what this ticket resolves.

**Attribution: `--class=preexisting --caused-by=ab74-b205-72af-4ce1` (epic rule-swamp-pupil).** `git blame -w -C -M -L168` traces the emit to `6119c24dedcd` 'feat(io): T2 — NDJSON export' (2026-06-17 21:31), the commit that introduced export_ndjson.py, under epic P1.2 rule-swamp-pupil (`ab74-b205-72af-4ce1`). That commit has no rebar-ticket trailer (predates the convention) but its body cites P1.2/rule-swamp-pupil. This is contract-evolution/preexisting: export always emitted bare ints since introduction. Note the >2^53 float64 hazard was ALREADY documented in-repo hours earlier the same day (`_store/canonical.py`, `_store/hlc.py`: 'jq must never touch it (it parses as float64 and rounds)', commits 1dbe5e7e 18:17 / cee1fe98 18:47) and that text is present in 6119c24's own tree — so the export feature re-exposed a known hazard at a new JSON boundary, a defect a reviewer of that epic could plausibly have caught. `--caused-by` supplied explicitly on close to override best-effort blame auto-derivation.

**Round-trip parity (in-scope).** The import twin (`import_ndjson.py` via `_io/_provenance.py`) reads `created_at`/`comments[].timestamp` verbatim into `source_created_at` provenance. Verified at runtime: feeding a decimal-STRING timestamp stores `source_created_at` as a str (digits preserved but type drifts int->str). Fix coerces with `int()` on import (rhino's reader pattern) so the store stays canonical regardless of wire form. Round-trip preserves EXACT ns digits.

**Escalation check: none.** Sole in-repo consumer of export NDJSON is `rebar import` (no backup/dump path). export.schema.json types timestamps as [integer,string] and states 'the projection can evolve without breaking consumers' — schema-conformant EXTERNAL consumers already must accept the string form; no concrete external consumer with a hard bare-int dependency exists. Proceeding as a correctness/parity fix; EXPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped + documented BREAKING per acceptance criteria.
